title: Tensor and finitely presented internal Hom under the small-etale module comparison
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use its Zariski and small etale sites [def-sc-zariski-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(u:V\to T)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. For a quasi-coherent Zariski module $M$ [pqf-def-coherent], let $A_T(M)=M_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the canonical associated module sheaf, $A_T(M)(u)=\Gamma(V,u^*M)$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module, def-pc-module-pullback]; use the canonical equivalence and its restriction comparisons [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Tensor products and sheaf Hom are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For quasi-coherent Zariski modules $M,N$, the canonical tensor comparison is an isomorphism
$$A_T(M)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}}A_T(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}N).$$
On local tensor sections it sends $m\otimes n$ to their tensor section after pullback. If $M$ is of finite presentation, meaning Zariski locally the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O^{\oplus a}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus b}$ with $a,b<\infty$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], then $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(M,N)$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent] and the canonical evaluation comparison is an isomorphism
$$A_T(\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(M,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}}(A_T(M),A_T(N)).$$
This comparison sends the image of a Zariski local module morphism to its associated etale morphism. Both comparisons are natural in their module arguments and commute with restriction to a further small-etale scheme object, under the canonical restriction and pullback comparisons of the cited equivalence. No Noetherian or separation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), parts (7),(8), only the small etale site, and their proof. The already-existing Zariski sheaf-Hom quasi-coherence lemma supplies the essential-image input.

proof.text: Put $L=\epsilon^*$. The cited equivalence identifies $L(F)$ with $A_T(F)$ for quasi-coherent $F$. The tensor product $M\otimes N$ is quasi-coherent by the cited tensor-closure theorem. Apply the ringed-topos tensor-pullback isomorphism to $\epsilon$, and invert its displayed direction, to obtain $A_T(M)\otimes A_T(N)\simeq A_T(M\otimes N)$. This is the canonical comparison: the defining balanced pairing for tensor pullback sends pulled-back local sections $m,n$ to the pullback of $m\otimes n$, with scalar coefficients multiplied. Indeed $(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)\mapsto st\otimes(m\otimes n)$ is balanced, and the reverse formula is $s\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$. The two composites are the identity by balancing; the formulas extend through sheafification. Thus this isomorphism has the section formula in the statement. The sites are taken small in the stipulated module universe.

Assume $M$ finitely presented and put $H=\mathcal Hom(M,N)$, which is quasi-coherent by the cited theorem. Its evaluation $H\otimes M\to N$ sends $h\otimes m$ to $h(m)$. Apply $A_T$ and compose with the tensor comparison of step 1. This gives an evaluation pairing $A_T(H)\otimes A_T(M)\to A_T(N)$. It defines a module map $\theta:A_T(H)\to\mathcal Hom(A_T(M),A_T(N))$ directly: for an etale object $U$ and $h\in A_T(H)(U)$, its component on $W\to U$ is $m\mapsto\mathrm{ev}_W(h|_W,m)$. Bilinearity gives module linearity and the restriction law of the pairing gives a morphism on the slice. This construction is exactly the evaluation comparison. On an associated Zariski morphism $h$ it gives the associated morphism, since $\mathrm{ev}(h,m)=h(m)$ before and after applying the functor.

source.place: Tag 06VE(8); sites-modules.tex Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), defining evaluation comparison.

proof.text: Work on a Zariski open $V$ with a presentation $\mathcal O_V^a\xrightarrow{B}\mathcal O_V^b\xrightarrow{p}M|_V\to0$, writing $B(e_k)=\sum_i b_{ik}e_i$. The finite-presentation Hom-kernel theorem identifies $H|_V$ with the kernel of $\alpha:(N|_V)^b\to(N|_V)^a$, $\alpha((x_i))_k=\sum_i b_{ik}x_i$, by $h\mapsto(h(p(e_i)))_i$. Apply $A_V$. It preserves finite sums: on all modules $\epsilon_V^*$ is a left adjoint by the module adjunction and hence preserves their coproducts; moreover $A_V(\mathcal O_V)=\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{et}}$ by the section formula. All finite sums in question are quasi-coherent. The image of $\alpha$ is quasi-coherent by the image theorem, so the short exact sequence $0\to H|_V\to(N|_V)^b\to\operatorname{im}\alpha\to0$ is a sequence of quasi-coherent modules. Exactness of $A_V$ and preservation of monomorphisms therefore identify $A_V(H|_V)$ with the kernel of the same matrix $\alpha_{\mathrm{et}}:(A_V(N|_V))^b\to(A_V(N|_V))^a$. Here the coefficients are the images of $b_{ik}$ in the etale structure sheaf. Likewise $A_V(p)$ is the cokernel of the associated presentation.

source.place: Tag 06VE(8), expanded finite-presentation kernel argument in sites-modules.tex Tag 0GN2 (lemma-pullback-internal-hom).

proof.text: Compute the target Hom on the same chart. Write $Q=A_V(M|_V)$ and $P=A_V(N|_V)$. For every $W$ of $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, slice restriction preserves the cokernel presentation $\mathcal O^a\to\mathcal O^b\to Q\to0$. A morphism $Q|_W\to P|_W$ is consequently a morphism $\mathcal O_W^b\to P|_W$ annihilating $B|_W$, uniquely, by the cokernel universal property. Such a map is uniquely specified by its basis images $x_i\in P(W)$: on any further object $Z\to W$ it sends $(r_i)_i$ to $\sum_i r_i x_i|_Z$. Annihilating the $k$th relation says precisely $\sum_i b_{ik}|_W x_i=0$. Thus evaluation on $p(e_i)$ gives a bijection between $\mathcal Hom(Q,P)(W)$ and $\ker(\alpha_{\mathrm{et}}(W))$. Both directions commute with restriction and scalar multiplication by these explicit formulas. Sectionwise kernels are sheaf kernels, so $\mathcal Hom(Q,P)$ is the kernel sheaf of $\alpha_{\mathrm{et}}$. This is an elementary cokernel calculation, not an appeal to exactness of sections of a cokernel.

source.place: Tag 06VE(8); sites-modules.tex Tag 0GN2, kernel rows, with the cokernel universal-property argument of Tag 0GMY (lemma-internal-hom-exact).

proof.text: Under the two kernel identifications, $\theta$ of step 2 is the identity: evaluating it on the image of the $i$th basis section is exactly the image of $h(p(e_i))$, by its evaluation formula. Thus $\theta$ is invertible over $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. These charts test the global map. In fact $T_{\mathrm{et}}/V=V_{\mathrm{et}}$: composition and cancellation of etale morphisms give the identical objects, arrows and coverings. The restriction comparisons of the equivalence identify $A_T(F)|_V$ with $A_V(F|_V)$; internal Hom restricts by its slice definition. The chosen Zariski opens cover every etale object after inverse image, since open immersions are etale. The local inverses agree on overlaps, being inverses to the same map $\theta$, and glue uniquely by the sheaf condition. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism globally. This uses arbitrary open overlaps, with no claim that intersections are affine.

source.place: Tag 06VE(8), local reduction in sites-modules.tex Tag 0GN2 and normalization of the equivalence.

proof.text: Finally check the asserted compatibilities of the actual maps. For module arrows $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, the tensor naturality square on local pure tensors sends $m\otimes n$ along either path to $f(m)\otimes g(n)$. These tensors locally generate the sheafified tensor, so the square commutes. For Hom, precomposition by $f:M'\to M$ and postcomposition by $g:N\to N'$ send a local transformation $h$ to $g h f$; evaluation on $m'$ along both paths is $g(h(f(m')))$. Equality on all slice objects proves equality of the Hom maps. For slice restriction, the tensor square sends $m\otimes n$ to the tensor of their restrictions along both paths, using the cited pure-tensor restriction isomorphism. The Hom square follows on every slice object from $(h(m))|_W=h|_W(m|_W)$. Consequently restricting the evaluation pairing and then forming the transformation on a slice is the same as forming that transformation after restriction. These are identities of pairings and transformations on all further objects, so they apply to every section, not only to a Zariski-origin section. The inverse isomorphisms inherit the same squares.

source.place: Tag 06VE(7),(8); sites-modules.tex Tags 03EL and 0GMX, natural pairings and slice restriction.

proof.text: To express the last restriction square using the scheme object $u:U\to T$, identify $T_{\mathrm{et}}/U$ with $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ by etale composition and cancellation. The equivalence supplies $A_T(F)|_U\simeq A_U(u^*F)$. Here $u^*M$ is finitely presented, and $u^*M,u^*N$ are quasi-coherent. There is also the required scheme Hom identification: $u$ is flat, so exact pullback carries the local matrix kernel for $H$ in step 3 to the kernel of that matrix with pulled-back coefficients; the finite-presentation Hom-kernel theorem applied on $U$ identifies this same kernel with $\mathcal Hom(u^*M,u^*N)$. The comparison is the evaluation comparison because both identifications send a map to its values on the same pulled-back generators. This is the three-line kernel consequence of the cited results (Modules Tag 0C6I), not an extra assumption on the comparison equivalence. Substituting these identifications into the slice square of step 6 gives exactly the requested small-etale scheme-object restriction square.

source.place: Tag 06VE(8), canonical restriction comparisons; modules.tex Tag 0C6I (lemma-pullback-internal-hom), finite-presentation kernel argument.
